## Bioinformatics, AI and Data Science Training 2026

**16–17 July 2026**

**Cresta Hotel, Somora Drive, Gaborone, Botswana**

*Hosted by the Botswana Harvard Partnership (BHP) and the Harvard T.H. Chan
School of Public Health (HSPH)*

## Overview

This two-day workshop will prepare you to bring bioinformatics, AI, and data
science to bear on real biological questions — and, just as importantly, to
recognise when they don't apply.

We start from first principles: what bioinformatics actually is, what people
mean when they say "AI", what data science adds, and whether you need all three.
These are not interchangeable words, and using them precisely is a research
skill in itself.

The focus of **Day 1** is machine learning applied to real biological data. You
will work through multi-OMICS profiling in HIV using advanced ML techniques,
including proteomics and metabolomics integration. The afternoon turns to AI in
medical research and the ethical considerations that come with it, then to a
practical integration and coding session.

The focus of **Day 2** is discovery and evolution. You will cover biomarker
discovery using bulk RNA-Seq, single cell multiome profiling in CD4 T cells,
and SIV/HIV integration site profiling. The afternoon moves to the principles
of viral evolution, phylogenetics, and phylodynamics, working hands-on with
AliView, IQ-TREE, FigTree, and BEAST.

A theme runs through both days: **a method always returns an answer, but it
cannot tell you whether your question was answerable.** The hands-on case study
uses a real Botswana cohort where a perfectly reasonable analysis produces a
result that cannot be interpreted — and finding out why is the lesson.

## Who is it for?

Anyone working with data in health and disease who wants a foundation in
bioinformatics and data science — and a working awareness of what AI can and
cannot do for their research. No command line experience necessary; some data
analysis in R is a plus.

::: {.grid}
::: {.g-col-6}
1. Research scientists
2. Medical practitioners and clinicians
3. Laboratory scientists and technologists
4. Postgraduate students (MSc, PhD)
5. Undergraduate students in the life sciences
6. Molecular biologists
7. Virologists and immunologists
8. Epidemiologists
:::
::: {.g-col-6}
9. Public health professionals
10. Biostatisticians and data analysts
11. Data managers
12. Early-career bioinformaticians
13. Clinical research staff and study coordinators
14. Pharmacists and pharmacologists
15. Lecturers and academic staff

## Prework

Two things before you arrive:

1. **Complete the [PreAssessment](https://forms.cloud.microsoft/r/zmADzApJ7v){target="_blank"}.**
   It takes a few minutes and tells us who is in the room.

2. **Install the software.** Bring a laptop with R, RStudio, and the Day 2
   tools (AliView, IQ-TREE 3, FigTree 1.4.4, BEAST 1.10.5) already installed —
   see [Installation](installation-instructions.qmd) for step-by-step
   instructions.

::: {.callout-tip}
## Install before you travel
Mr. Sabone runs a setup session at 9:00 on both mornings, but the downloads are
large and conference wifi is not. Arriving with software installed will save
you an hour and let you spend it on the science instead.
:::

If you have a dataset and a question from your own work, bring those too.

## Software

R · RStudio · AliView · IQ-TREE 3 · FigTree 1.4.4 · BEAST 1.10.5

All are free and open source. See [Installation](installation-instructions.qmd).

## Instructors

**Prof. Malika** leads the multi-OMICS and machine learning sessions, covering
proteomics and metabolomics integration, bulk RNA-Seq biomarker discovery,
single cell multiome profiling, and SIV/HIV integration site analysis.

**Dr. Wonderful T. Choga** is a bioinformatics scientist working on viral
genomics in Botswana, with research spanning hepatitis B virus genomics,
HIV drug resistance, and mitochondrial genetics. He was Course Organizer for
the 2025 Virus Evolution and Genomics Workshop and leads the sessions on AI in
medical research and ethics, viral evolution, phylogenetics, and
phylodynamics.

**Prof. Khei** is the Training and Development Manager at the Botswana Harvard
Partnership and opens and closes both days.

**Mr. Phenyo Sabone** provides technical support and runs the software
installation sessions.

See [About](about.qmd) for the full teaching team and our
[past workshops](past_workshops.qmd).
